prompt:
Use $text-composition in nonfiction-drafting mode from .agents/skills/text-composition/SKILL.md.

Write a complete 220–300-word explanatory article for residents about a neighborhood library survey. Supplied facts: 30 people responded; 18 reported weekly use; recruitment occurred only at the library entrance on one Saturday; no citywide comparison exists. Discuss what can and cannot be learned. You may use an explicitly hypothetical example, but there are no interviews, quotations, or other studies in the packet.

args:
developer_instructions="Use $text-composition in `nonfiction-drafting` mode. If unavailable, use the intake, domain decisions, verification, and output contract below as the bounded fallback.
Identify the reader question, thesis, category, extent, evidence packet, and citation expectations. Write the complete requested text with a distinct purpose for each section and meaningful transitions.
Track documented fact, memory, interpretation, hypothetical illustration, and open source needs. Preserve comparison groups, units, chronology, uncertainty, and causal scope. Never turn a paraphrase into an invented quotation or add personal experiences or credentials for the author.
Missing facts can be queried, qualified, or omitted while the draft proceeds. Missing packet details do not prove that an underlying study omitted a question, method, or result; limit negative claims to the supplied evidence. Check core claims against supplied locations and report what remains unverified. Do not replace a requested full draft with an outline; mark actual remaining units for long work.
Inspect assigned files before editing, preserve concurrent edits and source originals, and apply changes only within the requested artifact scope. Full drafting and rewriting are supported when requested.
Use `nonfiction-manuscript-editor` for thesis and chapter architecture, `fact-checking-editor` for verification, `citation-integrity-checker` for citations, and `line-copy-editor` for the later copy pass.
Return exactly these sections: `Draft`, `Source And Claim Notes`, `Editorial Decisions`, `Coverage And Checks`, `Open Queries`, `Files Changed`, `Handoffs`.
"

commands.command:
/bin/bash -lc "article_text='What This Library Survey Can—and Cannot—Tell Us

Thirty people responded to a recent neighborhood library survey, and 18 of them reported using the library weekly. That result describes the answers received: 18 of 30 respondents—60 percent—reported weekly use. It is a useful snapshot of the people reached that day, showing that regular users were represented among the respondents.

The recruitment method matters. The survey was conducted only at the library entrance on one Saturday. Every respondent was therefore already at the library when approached. This group is not the same as all neighborhood residents: it leaves out residents who did not visit during that place and time. The result cannot estimate how often all neighborhood residents use the library, or show whether weekly use is common among people who rarely or never come to the building.

Nor can these results establish how this neighborhood compares with the city as a whole. No citywide comparison is available in the supplied information, so the survey does not show whether this response pattern is higher, lower, or similar to use elsewhere.

The findings can still help identify the next question. For example, a future survey could invite people at several neighborhood locations and through several channels, then compare answers by recruitment method. This is a hypothetical approach, not evidence about current library use. It could produce a different mix of respondents, but it would not change what the Saturday entrance survey recorded.

For now, residents can read the survey as a small, location-specific account of its participants: 18 reported weekly library use. It is a starting point for further inquiry, not a measure of the neighborhood or citywide population.'
printf '%s' \""'$article_text" | wc -w
find outputs -maxdepth 1 -type f -printf '"'%p\\n'"

disposition: Content failure: described an undated survey as recent. Added unsupported-specificity and relationship checks and reran.
